title: SPEC: board analytics + HTML report — derive views from tasks/events JSONL, define UX (collapse-first), streak semantics
reasoning: SPEC-FIRST TASK (worker writes the spec, then implements in follow-ups). Goal: boardctl renders boards into a static HTML report + optional loopback server so anyone can drop a board folder or zip (multi-board) and see project progress. DATA MODEL (all derivable from tasks.jsonl + events.jsonl + board.jsonl header — no git/repo access needed, uploaded boards must work): (1) task rows: sparse-key tolerant parse, id/title/status/priority/primary_model/commit_hash/reasoning/worker_summary/guard_result/ci_result/attempts/completed_at; fixture rows = id NEVER-DONE* or perpetual:true — EXCLUDED from burndown/velocity/streaks per SCHED-GAP-106 doctrine but visible in task list behind a toggle. (2) event rows: id/timestamp/event_type/task_id/actor/detail/tick_number; tolerant of torn trailing line. (3) timestamps: boards historically use '2006-01-02 15:04:05' AND RFC3339 — parse both. DERIVED VIEWS (each answers a user question): burndown (open tasks/day — backlog shrinking?), burn-up (cumulative completions — velocity, often more honest), weekly velocity bars, cycle time per task (created→done: median, p90, worst-5 table), streaks, tick-health timeline (completed/failed/audit per day), work clock (weekday×hour heatmap), model share over completed tasks, multi-board compare (overlaid burn-up, velocity race, side-by-side key numbers incl. ticks_total/ticks_idle). STREAK SEMANTICS (Bane: what days in a row must not be gameable): DeliveryStreak = consecutive days with >=1 real task completion (headline metric, current+longest); ActivityStreak = days with any non-noise event (current+longest); raw any-tick streak shown only as context, never headline. Render as GitHub-style calendar heatmap (day cells, intensity = event count, last 26 weeks). UX (Bane 163849): 3 layers — overview card grid (per-board mini sparkline + key numbers); project page (charts + task table); task rows COLLAPSED by default showing id/title/status chip/priority/model/commit, click expands in place to full detail (reasoning, worker summary, guard/ci verdicts, attempts, timestamps, last-8 related events, full JSON), expand/collapse-all, filters (text/status/fixtures toggle), expanded row addressable via URL hash. Constraints: single self-contained HTML, inline CSS/JS, NO CDN (works from file://), hand-rolled SVG charts (no libs), JSON island payload with </ escaping. Deliverable for this task: docs/specs/board-analytics-report.md covering data contracts, derivations, view catalog, UX spec, and acceptance criteria for BT-020/021/022.

title: header --set-* on a HEADERLESS board writes header counters INTO the first task row (bit: 9 keys -> 10 on CHT-001)
reasoning:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 while adding the worktree/branch/sessions fields.

REPRO (on a copy, never the live board):
  1. board with tasks.jsonl + events.jsonl and NO board.jsonl (real case: /home/kara/coding-hermes-tools/.coding-hermes/board/).
  2. `boardctl -C <board> header --set-ticks-total 90`
  3. prints: header updated (line 1 of tasks.jsonl): ticks_total, updated_at
  4. RESULT: task CHT-001 (the FIRST task row) grew from 9 keys to 10 -- it now carries ticks_total:90 and a rewritten updated_at. A real task row was silently mutated by a header operation.

ROOT CAUSE: with no board.jsonl the topology detection falls back to 'header = line 1 of tasks.jsonl' and never checks that line 1 is header-SHAPED. Line 1 here is an ordinary task row (id/title/status), so the write lands in a task.

SAME ROOT CAUSE, second symptom: `boardctl validate` on that board reports 3 false errors -- 'tasks.jsonl header: version / ticks_total / ticks_idle is not an integer counter' -- because it validates a task row as a header.

IMPACT: the tool whose entire contract is byte-preserving surgery on non-target rows silently rewrites one. Any headerless board in the fleet is one `header --set-*` away from a corrupted first row.

FIX SHAPE: when board.jsonl is absent, or line 1 carries task keys (id/title/status), classify the board HEADERLESS: (a) `header --set-*` must refuse with an explicit 'no header on this board' error instead of writing; (b) `validate` reports an informational 'headerless board (no board.jsonl)' line rather than integer-counter errors; (c) hard guard -- never write a header key into a row that also carries id/title/status. Tests: a headerless fixture for both paths, plus a RED proof that the guard fires.
worker_summary: header --set-* now refuses on headerless boards (no board.jsonl AND line 1 not header-shaped) with an explicit 'no header on this board' error (ErrNoHeader); validate/doctor emit one informational headerless line and skip the false integer-counter errors; rowIsTaskShape hard guard blocks header keys in any id/title/status row. 17 new tests (bt037_headerless_test.go x10, bt037_headerless_cli_test.go x7), RED-proven by disabling the guards (12 failures with the exact pre-fix symptoms). Foreman live probe on a copy of the real coding-hermes-tools board: header --set-ticks-total 90 -> exit 1, tasks.jsonl sha256 byte-identical, CHT-001 still 9 keys; validate exit 0 with zero false counter errors.

title: serve accumulates every upload in memory for the life of the process: re-uploading the same boards duplicates them in the report, /api/boards and the compare view
reasoning:
MEASURED 2026-09-20 (dogfood run, serve surface).
REPRO: boardctl serve -C <repo> in a browser; upload the SAME two-board zip three times.

The rendered report's compare table then lists boardctl TWICE side by side and the report banner reads 'Loaded boardctl, boardctl, b2 with 30 parse warnings'. Root cause: cmd/boardctl/serve.go:366 appends every upload session to s.sessions and currentBoards() (serve.go:201-207) concatenates ALL sessions plus cBoards on every request; nothing dedupes by board dir/slug and no route resets the set.

FIX DIRECTION: key loaded boards by resolved dir (replace on re-upload), and/or add an explicit reset (button + route) and document the lifetime in the README serve section. Decide and document whether -C should appear once when it is also uploaded.

title: Report parser rejects the colon-less UTC-offset dialect (-0500) that boardctl's OWN timestamp detector accepts, silently dropping rows from time-based metrics
reasoning:
MEASURED 2026-09-20 (dogfood run, render surface).
REPRO: render a board carrying created_at '2026-09-18T03:47:31-0500' (the dialect internal/board/timefmt.go zoneRe explicitly accepts and preserves: zoneRe = [+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}$; see coding-hermes-tools .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl line 1 and 3 more rows).
EVIDENCE: boardctl -C <board> render --json -> parse_warnings.timestamp_excluded counts those rows and the notes list "unparseable created_at \"2026-09-18T03:47:31-0500\" - excluded from time-based metrics". internal/render/load.go:507 stampLayouts has only two offset forms (Z07:00 with and without a fraction) - none accepts a -0500 offset - so parseStamp (load.go:522) returns ok=false. In the 3-board serve report the b2 board showed 30 excluded timestamps and its velocity collapsed to a single week while its tasks span several.
SCOPE (measured across 52 fleet boards, 8034 task rows): 4 rows on 1 board carry the literal -NNNN form, BUT the blast radius is larger than those rows because the same gap can silently zero a whole board's time series when the dialect is used for created_at/updated_at.
WHY IT MATTERS: boardctl ships the inverse rule - the detector accepts and PRESERVES -0500, but its own report parser cannot read it back. A writer/reader round trip inside one tool that loses data is a trust defect, not a cosmetic one. (Verified the writer itself is safe: boardctl create up-converts to +00:00, so the asymmetry is read-side only.)
FIX DIRECTION: add '2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z0700' and '2006-01-02T15:04:05Z0700' to stampLayouts, and add a table test pairing DetectTSLayout's accepted dialects with parseStamp so the two lists cannot drift apart again.

title: Usage errors print a literal backslash-n into the message, and subcommand usage output collides with its own exit line on one line
reasoning:

FIX DIRECTION: emit the usage block with a real newline (or two separate writes) and keep the error line separate.

title: CLI contract: `<cmd> --help` exits 1 (the documented validation-failure code) on every subcommand, and `event` with no --type silently appends an audit event instead of refusing
reasoning:
MEASURED 2026-09-21 (PM cycle; published v0.1.7 asset, fresh temp board, 13 subcommands probed):
(a) `boardctl <cmd> --help` exits 1 for every subcommand (create/update/event/header/show/list/import/render/serve/init/validate/doctor/stats) — the flag package's ErrHelp path flows out as a plain error — while bare `help` and `--help` exit 0. Any wrapper that classifies exit 1 as "validation failure" (README:192 "Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 validation failure, 2 usage/board-not-found") reads a help request as a failed board validation.
(b) `boardctl event` with NO --type is not refused: it appends {"event_type":"audit","timestamp":...,"actor":"foreman"} and exits 0, while the subcommand's own usage line (cmd/boardctl/main.go:653) advertises `event --type audit [flags]` and `event --type bogus` IS refused (exit 1, vocabulary listed). title: boardctl install: a git pre-commit hook that REJECTS a bad board (duplicate id / dangling ref), chained with the existing GitReins hook and bounded by a 30s timeout that SKIPS instead of blocking
reasoning:
WHAT AND WHY
A user who clones boardctl from GitHub, or runs it in a fleet repo, gets the
tool but NOT the protection: a board carrying a duplicate id or a dangling
depends_on reference can still be committed, and the damage only surfaces
later when a reader chokes on it. `boardctl validate` already detects every
one of these classes — nothing runs it at the moment a bad board would land.
This row is about TIMING, not detection.

EVIDENCE (2026-09-23, measured)
- `boardctl validate` on a healthy board: "RESULT: OK (0 warning(s))", exit 0.
  On the board damaged by the canopy incident it returned
  `[error] tasks.jsonl line 386: duplicate task id "DF-HERMES-CANOPY-52"
  (also line 382)` -> "RESULT: FAIL (1 error, 35 warnings)", exit 1.
  The detector exists, works, and names line numbers.
- BT-050 (open, P2) documents the writers that bypass `boardctl create`, and
  create ALREADY refuses a duplicate id (exit 2). So the guard is complete;
  it simply never runs at commit time.
- Fleet census 2026-09-23: **71 of 96** repos under /home/kara already carry
  `.git/hooks/pre-commit` — the GitReins Tier-1 hook, generated by
  `gitreins install`, whose binary path is PINNED at install time and which
  ends in a bare `exit $?`. Git allows exactly ONE pre-commit file, so a
  naive installer either clobbers that guard or gets clobbered by it.
  CHAINING IS THE CORE CONSTRAINT OF THIS ROW, not an option.

DELIVERABLE (tests-first per repo doctrine, with a RED ledger entry)
1. `boardctl hook run` — the hook's logic as a GO VERB, so it is testable
   rather than shell:
   - resolves the board like the sibling verbs (-C / repo root / board dir).
   - SKIPS CLEANLY (exit 0, one-line notice) when: not a board repo; the
     board file is absent; the boardctl binary cannot be resolved; or the
     staged set contains no board file (`--always` lints unconditionally).
     A hook that fails a commit because the tool is missing is worse than
     no hook at all.
   - STRICT lint on the staged board: duplicate id, dangling depends_on
     reference, unparseable line, out-of-vocabulary status -> FAIL (exit 1,
     naming the line numbers and the offending ids). The softer classes
     (priority vocabulary, legacy warnings) stay WARN and do NOT block.
   - BOUNDED: `--timeout` default **30s**; an expiry is exit 0 plus a loud
     SKIP notice. Rationale: the box may be saturated with running agents or
     the board may be large, and a lint hook must never wedge a commit.
   - Escape hatches, documented rather than hidden: `BOARDCTL_HOOK_SKIP=1`
     and `git commit --no-verify`.
2. `boardctl install [--hook] [--uninstall] [--force] [--global]`:
   - CHAINS: detect an existing pre-commit (the GitReins hook, or anything
     else), preserve it verbatim, and install a dispatcher that runs each
     hook in order and aggregates exit codes. The board-lint step runs FIRST
     so it reports before the slower guard. Never overwrite without --force.
   - `--global`: install once into a shared directory and point
     `core.hooksPath` at it, so a machine covers future clones; the per-repo
     install stays available.
   - Idempotent and reversible: a re-run is a no-op, `--uninstall` restores
     the previous hook byte-for-byte.
3. The "easy to add to repos" bundle: an example script under `examples/`,
   a README section showing `boardctl install` in three lines, and a SKILL
   that agents load stating the hook contract (what blocks, what warns, what
   skips) so a foreman that hits a rejection knows the REPAIR path instead of
   reflexively reaching for --no-verify.
4. A fleet-rollout mode for BT-053 to consume: install across many repos,
   report a per-repo outcome, never clobber.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- a duplicate id in the staged board -> `git commit` is REJECTED; the message
  names the id and both line numbers; `--no-verify` still works
- a dangling depends_on reference -> the same rejection path
- a clean board -> the commit proceeds unchanged
- no board / no binary / no board file staged -> exit 0, skip notice, commit
  proceeds
- lint exceeding the timeout (forced via a 1s `--timeout`) -> exit 0 + SKIP
  notice, commit proceeds
- in a repo carrying the GitReins hook, after install BOTH hooks run (prove
  the gitreins guard still blocks when its own config says it should), and
  `--uninstall` restores the original hook byte-identically
- re-running `boardctl install` is a no-op (no duplicated block, no diff)
- hermetic tests (no network, no real gitreins) pin every line above

SCOPE NOTE: the vocabulary of which validate classes are errors lives in
`validate` and must stay in ONE place — this row consumes it, never forks it.

title: validate silently yields nil for a non-array depends_on, so a dependency expressed in the wrong shape is invisible (BT-035 carries the string "[]")
reasoning:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while filing BT-052/053/054 (the board-lint pre-commit hook work),
so it belongs to that family rather than to a new investigation.

EVIDENCE
- Exactly ONE row on this board has a depends_on that is not an array: BT-035,
  which carries the STRING "[]" instead of an empty array. Every other row is
  either a real array or the key is absent.
- The tolerance is deliberate and documented in prose:
  internal/board/validate.go:220 — "depends_on). Non-array / malformed values
  yield nil." — and validate.go:171 feeds rowStringSlice(row, "depends_on") into
  the existence cross-check. A non-array therefore yields NO dependencies, the
  cross-check has nothing to test, and `boardctl validate` reports
  "RESULT: OK (0 warning(s))" for BT-035.
- The WRITE side is strict: internal/board/write.go:141 types DependsOn as
  []string, so boardctl's own writer could never emit this shape. This is
  legacy or hand-written data, exactly the population BT-050 describes.

WHY IT MATTERS (the class, not the single row)
The whole point of BT-054's hook is to stop a board carrying bad data from being
committed. A dependency expressed as a string is bad data that today round-trips
as "no dependencies" — silently. The failure is invisible in precisely the case
that hurts: if a row used the malformed shape with a REAL reference
("depends_on": "BT-019"), validate would emit no dangling-ref warning and a
reader would never see the edge at all. Tolerating the shape on READ is
defensible; tolerating it SILENTLY is not.

DELIVERABLE (small)
Add the class to `validate` (or to BT-054's strict lint) as a WARN:
"tasks.jsonl line N (task ID): depends_on is not an array — treated as no
dependencies". WARN and not error, so it cannot block a commit on legacy data by
itself; BT-054's hook owns the exit policy.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `boardctl validate` emits the new warning for BT-035 and still exits 0
- correcting BT-035 to [] makes the warning disappear
- a row with a real-but-malformed ref ("depends_on": "BT-019") is caught by the
  SAME warning — that is the case that actually protects a dependency edge
- no change to the existing dangling-ref check (BT-007 behaviour) and no new
  error introduced on any other row in this repo

reasoning: FOUND 2026-09-23 while auditing my own instrument rather than the boards. Checked all 11 candidates against 57 boards / 8,443 parsed rows, comparing rows that carry BOTH the alias and its target. FOUR REMOVED: (1) commit -> commit_hash: 6 rows carry it and TWO carry commit_hash with a DIFFERENT value (commit=afffb64 vs commit_hash=9b4536e on crier CI-001) - two different commits, so the rename would have rewritten which-commit on a row that legitimately says two things; (2) deps -> depends_on: 7 rows, every value the EMPTY STRING and no depends_on anywhere - the rename puts a string where the canon expects a list of ids; (3) review_otes -> review_notes: 2 rows, 100% conflict, and the values are DIFFERENT KINDS - review_otes holds captured cell output as prose while review_notes on the same rows holds provenance notes (id-renumbered records) - THIS ALSO CORRECTS BT-056, whose text calls review_otes an outright typo of review_notes; (4) review_notes_dupe: a candidate I invented that matched no row at all. title: P2 — create's key schema is computed from the board's own rows, so a drifted board makes every NEW row inherit its drift (observed: repo:null emitted on SCHED-GAP-1575)
reasoning: OBSERVED 2026-09-23 while filing a P1 on the scheduler board. boardctl create SCHED-GAP-1575 emitted a row containing repo:null, and validate then flagged it: 'key(s) {repo} outside the declared canon'. Nothing in my create call asked for repo. The mechanism is by design and is the problem: the create schema is the create-time default set UNION the extras MEASURED FROM THAT BOARD's existing rows (the same union that feeds the key-uniformity census), so on a board that already carries drift, every new row written through the tool inherits that drift and validates with a warning. Compare GAP-145 created the same way on the bunker board minutes earlier: no repo key, because bunker's rows do not carry one. WHY IT MATTERS: the tool exists to STOP drift spreading; a write path that mirrors the drift it is measuring makes the census self-perpetuating - repairing the old rows does not stop new ones being born dirty, and a board can never reach zero drift while any legacy row carries an extra key. It also weakens the census as evidence: 'N rows drift' partly counts rows the tool itself created. SUGGESTED FIX: separate the two sets explicitly - keep a canonical create schema (what a new row SHOULD carry) apart from the measured census (what rows DO carry), and have create write only the canonical schema, leaving the census to report the difference. If a board's extra key is deliberate, it belongs in the canon (like labels, sanctioned 2026-09-23) or in the alias table - not silently inherited. ALSO SEEN while checking, filed here rather than as its own row because it is the same class: that board's SECOND validator error, 'board.jsonl line 1: EOF', is a FORMAT error - the file is pretty-printed JSON spanning many lines while the validator reads JSONL (one object per line), so line 1 can never parse. Both that error and 'duplicate task id INT-CI-006' are pre-existing (verified against the committed board: same 2 errors, 287 warnings), i.e. this row added none.

title: P2 — README quickstart's `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` fails verbatim on a bare download (asset must keep its release filename)
reasoning: OBSERVED 2026-09-24 (dogfood run 15, fresh Debian 13 bunker agent 2909fec1). Docs-only fix.

title: P2 REPO-HYGIENE: this repo tracks .coding-hermes/board/board.db, so its own doctor FAILs (git-tracked-set error) — and TestDoctorRepoBoardNoTrackedCaches skips .db files, so the tracked case is ungated
reasoning:

  $ ./bin/boardctl doctor -C .
  [error] git-tracked-set: .coding-hermes/board/board.db is tracked under .coding-hermes/board — JSONL-canonical boards must not track db/parquet caches
  RESULT: FAIL (1 error(s), 10 warning(s))

  => the 12KB board.db cache was ADDED by an unrelated errcheck commit; no commit ever intended to track it.
  $ grep -n board .gitignore
  8:.coding-hermes/board/.lock      <-- only the lock is ignored; board.db is NOT
  $ ls -la .coding-hermes/board/board.db -> 12288 bytes, mtime 2026-10-12 05:43

WHY IT MATTERS: the repo whose contract is JSONL-canonical boards (and whose doctor exists to police exactly this: df-boardctl-35 made tracked caches an ERROR and untracked fossils a warning) fails its own gate. docs/dogfood/diagnostics.md:288 already states the rule ("The board files are git-tracked — NEVER commit a board.db/*.parquet"); the live repo breaks it. Any consumer that reads doctor status as green is misreading a FAIL.

THE UNGATED HALF (why no test caught it): internal/board/doctor_test.go:266 TestDoctorRepoBoardNoTrackedCaches deliberately SKIPS .db/.parquet entries when copying the live board into a fresh git repo (lines 282-284: "the live board dir may carry an UNTRACKED cache"). That skip was written for the untracked-fossil case, and it also masks the TRACKED case — so a committed board.db is invisible to the suite while doctor errors in production. A test that consults the REAL tracked set (e.g. `git ls-files .coding-hermes/board` from the module root and assert no .db/.parquet) closes the blind spot; TestDoctorGitTrackedDBError (line 305) already proves the detector itself works on a synthetic board.

FIX DIRECTION (2 files + 1 test):
  1. `git rm --cached .coding-hermes/board/board.db` (keep the local file; it is a retired cache — doctor calls such fossils "safe-to-remove caches").
  2. .gitignore: ignore .coding-hermes/board/*.db and *.parquet (belt-and-braces vs. a future `git add -A`).
  3. Replace/extend TestDoctorRepoBoardNoTrackedCaches with an assertion over the live git-tracked set so the tracked case can never regress silently.
ACCEPTANCE: `./bin/boardctl doctor -C .` on a fresh clone reports 0 errors (the board.db line becomes a warning or disappears); `git ls-files .coding-hermes/board/` lists only the four JSONL files; the new test FAILS on a repo that tracks a board.db (RED-proven) and passes at HEAD.

title: normalize-board --apply silently DROPS a task row created while it runs — the write lock wraps only the rewrite, not the read/classify — and validate/doctor stay green while the row's task_created event is left orphaned
reasoning:
Dogfood run 25 (tick boardctl-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-52-34), SECOND delivery of the tick; reproduced at HEAD 900b7b5 (built from a clean checkout copy, `boardctl version dev`) AND on the RELEASED v0.1.11 binary — identical behaviour, so this is product code, not deployment drift.

PROBE (decisive, both binaries): board with 20,000 drifted rows (so --apply has work). CONTROL: `create --id CTRL-1` with no apply running -> rc=0, row present. TREATMENT: start `normalize-board --apply`, wait 0.6s (apply already past its read), run `create --id PROBE-MID-1` -> rc=0 'created task PROBE-MID-1 (appended to .../tasks.jsonl)', row IS present in tasks.jsonl while the apply is still running, and GONE after the apply finishes. apply rc=0, prints a successful 'applied' rewrite. events.jsonl keeps the probe's task_created event (1 match) while tasks.jsonl has 0 -> orphan event. Bulk rows intact 20000/20000, so the loss is specific to the concurrent append, not general damage.

REPEATED: 8 rounds x 20 concurrent creates = 160 creates, every one rc=0 'created task', 0 present afterwards (unparseable lines 0, duplicate ids 0). A fleet lane writing while an operator/foreman runs the repair loses every row it wrote during the window, silently.

MECHANISM (source, both same at HEAD and in the v0.1.11 tag): internal/board/normalizeboard.go NormalizeBoard(apply) reads tasks.jsonl and classifies every line FIRST (the read/classify pass ends at the rewritten-bytes assembly around line 400), and only then acquires the write guard at normalizeboard.go:418-421, which wraps nothing but atomicRewrite(tasksPath, rewritten). So the lock covers the write, not the check-then-act window. internal/board/lock.go:17-19 states the guard exists precisely to prevent this ('read-modify-write rewrites ... silently drop the winner's change'), and README:1256-1259 tells users 'every write verb takes an exclusive advisory flock ... for its whole check-then-act window'. For this verb the documentation and the code disagree.

SILENCE: after the loss, `validate` -> rc=0, 'RESULT: OK (0 warning(s))', 20002 rows; `doctor` -> rc=0. Nothing reconciles events against rows, so the operator sees a green board that is missing a row they watched being created.

WINDOW SCALES WITH BOARD SIZE (hyperfine --warmup 1 --runs 5, HEAD build, `normalize-board --apply` re-applied each run): 1,000 rows 16.0 ms +/- 5.8; 10,000 rows 84.3 ms +/- 9.4; 50,000 rows 346.2 ms +/- 25.6. On a real second-scale repair of a big board the window is not a theoretical race.

TEST GAP: internal/board/write_concurrency_test.go has 7 tests and every one is append-vs-append, same-id racing, lock exclusivity/release, or reader isolation. No test interleaves a rewrite with an append, which is why this shipped.

Repro artifacts (this tick's scratch, discarded): /tmp/df1023/repro.sh (decisive control/treatment), /tmp/df1023/conc.sh (8x20 concurrent), /tmp/df1023/measure_rewrite.sh (the sizing numbers).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A create that lands while a rewrite verb is running is still present after the verb exits: the read/classify pass for NormalizeBoard (and RepairEvents, DedupeByID) runs INSIDE the same write guard as its write, or the rewrite re-reads the file under the guard and merges rows it did not classify (no lost append). 2) A regression test in internal/board/write_concurrency_test.go interleaves an append with each rewrite verb and asserts the appended row/event survives; the test FAILS on the current tree and passes after the fix (prove both directions). 3) The same test asserts no orphan task_created event is produced. 4) If serializing the whole verb is rejected as a design choice, the command must instead detect a concurrent append (the byte-comparison refusal internal/board/repair.go:129-142 already implements) and refuse with a precise message, and README:1256-1259 must stop claiming the lock covers 'its whole check-then-act window'. 5) `go test ./...` exits 0.

title: P4 — README claims CI's Go 1.26 toolchain is sufficient while go.mod requires Go 1.26.10
reasoning:
Doc severity P4 by Bane's 2026-09-30 ruling: documentation findings are P4/P5, not P1-P3; this policy is not a new assessment of the underlying toolchain risk.

FINDING: README.md:1493-1501 says the toolchain requirement is `go 1.26.10`, but .github/workflows/ci.yml:15 runs the full CI job with `go-version: ["1.26"]`. On GitHub Actions, setup-go resolves that moving minor line independently of the README's patch requirement, so the README does not tell a stranger the actual CI toolchain floor or how CI obtains 1.26.10.

EXACT COMMANDS AND OUTPUT:
`grep -nE 'go-version|go 1\.26' README.md .github/workflows/ci.yml go.mod` -> README.md:1493: The toolchain requirement: go.mod declares `go 1.26.10`; .github/workflows/ci.yml:15: go-version: ["1.26"]; go.mod:3: go 1.26.10.
`sed -n '12,28p' .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> CI configures setup-go with `go-version: ["1.26"]`, not `1.26.10`.
`go version` -> go1.26.10 linux/amd64 for this local probe; no older Go toolchain was installed to exercise the refusal branch.

FIX: reconcile the README and CI contract: either pin CI to `1.26.10` and state that exact floor, or document the moving `1.26` CI resolution and separately explain how the patched 1.26.10 requirement is enforced. Add a reproducible parity check so the two files cannot drift.

ACCEPTANCE: the README toolchain paragraph, go.mod:3, and CI setup-go version express one verified policy; a fresh checkout can run the documented command and see the same floor.

UNVERIFIED: no older Go 1.26.x toolchain was available, so this sweep did not prove the exact failure behavior below 1.26.10.
